known_defects: v1: 3 bridges, 3 touching bends. The mux cross-connect forces one crossing, and the two ISP pairs feeding two MUXes weave around the MUX boxes. Reducing further would need a different split, and the per-view spec budget (3 candidates) was spent.
v2: 2 bridges, one per cross-connected tier. Each tier is a complete 2x2 fan, so one bridge per tier is structural, not sloppiness.
v3: 4 bridges. The border-leaf -> spine fan enters the spine boxes through side ports, so two routes cross near Spine 1 and two near Spine 2.

v3: the border-leaf -> spine and leaf -> rack links share the view, while the spine -> rack-leaf ECMP fan lives in v4. A reader who opens only v3 sees the spines connected to border leaves only; the coverage map names v4 for the rest.

v4: orientation is lr (spines in the source column), because the same fan rendered tb needed reserved spacer rows and still produced 2 ambiguous label owners. v3 owns the vertical spine-above-leaf layout the source asked for.
v1 and v2 are lr for the same reason: the tb renderings of both left a label with no unambiguous owner at the canvas edge (v1 attempt 1 and 2).

Group hues are not stable across views: core is pink in v1 and yellow in v2, edge is pink in v2 and aqua in v3, leaf is pink in v3 and aqua in v4. The spec format has no color field (only a group name), so cross-view color identity is not expressible; inside each view the families are distinct.
environment_notes: herdr pane layout returned no rect for the split pane, so manifest pane_rect/pane_cols are null in all four bundles; size and zoom are proven by the running app's own header token '77x47 @100%', which the validator accepts.
